authors: Sitan Chen, Weiyuan Gong, Jonas Haferkamp, Yihui Quek

statement: Remark 7 When d = ω(n2/3 ), we conjecture that quantum planted biclique is not just low-degree hard, but information-theoretically impossible with local measurements. Interestingly, we observe that in this regime, there is a low-degree algorithm based on non-local single-copy measurements which works provided λ = ω(n2/3 ) (see Lemma 64). We leave as an intriguing open question resolving the low-degree complexity of quantum planted biclique under non-local single-copy measurement strategies. For instance, is there such an algorithm that works even below λ ≍ n2/3 ? This would yield a fine-grained computational separation between local and non-local single-copy measurement strategies. Given the central role played by the planted clique conjecture within the classical literature on complexity of statistical inference, in particular the extensive web of reductions from this problem to other inference problems (Berthet and Rigollet, 2013; Brennan et al., 2018; Brennan and Bresler, 2020), our definition of the quantum version of this problem may also be of independent interest.

Q UANTUM HARDNESS FOR HYBRID AND CLASSICAL PROBLEMS . In the last part of this work, we explore whether the low-degree framework can also be used to establish quantum hardness for problems where a portion or all of the input is classical. Our first result along these lines concerns the Learning Stabilizers with Noise (LSN) problem (Poremba et al., 2024), recently proposed as a hybrid classical-quantum analogue of Learning Parity with Noise (LPN).
